sections.h2: Where to record a Madison County deed
sections.html:
The Madison County Recorder is at the courthouse in London: 1 N Main St, Room 40, London, OH 43140. Call 740-852-1854. The counter opens at 8 AM and closes at 4 PM on weekdays, though recording ends at 3:30 PM, so a deed handed over at 3:45 waits until the next business day.

Electronic recording runs through four platforms: CSC eRecording (866-652-0111), Simplifile, ePN and Hopdox. Ask your title company or attorney which one they use. The deed can then be recorded without a trip to the courthouse.

A two-page deed is $39.00 and each extra page is $8.00. Senate Bill 94 added a $5.00 surcharge to most documents to fund the preservation and digitizing of records and the office's running costs, under section 317.32.

That statute builds the amount from half a base fee, half a housing trust fund fee, plus an optional county surcharge. Copies, certified copies, references to older documents and zoning filings carry their own listed amounts. Phone 740-852-1854 to price any unusual document before you mail payment.

sections.h2: How far back the online land records reach
sections.html:
Different record types start at different dates. Checking the right category saves a trip to the courthouse.

Online coverage by record type, Madison County Recorder
Record typeOnline coverage
DeedsScanned, indexed and online from March 1, 1920 to present
Mortgages, indexingIndexed from July 17, 1964
Mortgages, imagesScanned and indexed from September 25, 1968
Miscellaneous, lease, lien, federal tax lien, mechanics lien, unemployment compensation lien, mortgage releaseHistorical Archive online, dating to at least 1980, some older

All the original books remain in the office. If a search turns up a gap, call the counter and ask staff to follow up in the books.

sections.h2: What the Auditor does with a deed first
sections.html:
Ohio makes the Auditor endorse the deed before the Recorder files it. Under section 319.202, the buyer's representative submits a statement of value, or a statement of the exemption reason, and the Auditor notes the conveyance fee on the deed itself.

The Madison County Auditor is at 1 N Main St, PO Box 47, London, OH 43140-0047, phone 740-852-9717, weekdays 8 AM to 4 PM. The property transfer forms page lists the packet pieces a closer may need:

  • DTE 100, the conveyance fee statement of value and receipt.
  • DTE 100EX, the statement of the reason for an exemption.
  • DTE 101, a statement of conveyance of homestead property.
  • DTE 102, a statement of conveyance of current agricultural use valuation property.
  • DTE 100M and DTE 41 for manufactured or mobile homes.
  • Affidavits of trustee and successor trustee under sections 317.22 and 5302.171.

The Auditor's site also carries a conveyance fee calculator under its Tools menu. Run your sale through it, or phone the office, rather than guessing at the county's rate.

sections.h2: Sale price, gifts and the value statement
sections.html:
For an arm's length sale, the measure under section 319.202 is everything paid or promised, including any mortgage balance the buyer takes over. For a gift, the measure shifts to what the house would sell for on the open market. Misstating either figure on purpose is unlawful.

The buyer's statement also answers two questions. Was the seller asked whether tax reductions for owner occupancy or homestead apply? Was the land under the agricultural use valuation? A yes to either needs a sworn instrument attached. If the house is a rental, the endorsement points the buyer to a landlord filing under section 5323.02.

sections.h2: Free tools on the Auditor's website
sections.html:
The Auditor's home page lets you search any parcel by owner, address or parcel number to see its appraisal and payment history. A menu of tools sits beside the search box, and several help a seller price and plan:

  • A sales report and a sales list of recent transfers.
  • A delinquency report.
  • A conveyance fee calculator and a tax estimator.
  • A levy estimator, plus a GIS parcel viewer reached from the map link.

Two statutes work together. Section 319.54(G)(3) sets the state charge at a dollar or a dime per hundred, whichever is bigger. Section 322.02 lets commissioners layer on a local tax up to thirty cents per hundred, owed by the grantor.

Exemptions cover several family and estate situations:

  • Gifts within a marriage, or handed down to a son or daughter.
  • Transfers among the heirs of one decedent when nobody pays money.
  • Moves into or out of a revocable trust.
  • A corrective deed that fixes an earlier recorded deed.

The exemption reason belongs on the form. Without it the Auditor will not stamp the deed as exempt, and the Recorder will not accept a deed that skipped the Auditor.

sections.h2: Madison County housing and the 2026 reappraisal
sections.html: Madison County lies in central Ohio west of Franklin County, with London as the seat and largest city. Population was 46,985 in mid-2025, up 7.1 percent since 2020, with 17,383 housing units. A typical owned home is valued at $250,100, owners occupy 77.5 percent of homes, and rent runs a median $943. The Auditor has finished a countywide reappraisal for tax year 2026, with tentative values shown for each parcel on its website, so look up your own parcel before setting a price.

Neighbors include Union and Champaign counties to the north and northwest, Franklin County to the east, Pickaway to the southeast, Fayette to the south, and Greene and Clark to the west. An owner with land across a county line needs a separate recorder and auditor filing in each county.

Putting the sale together

The title company or attorney prepares the deed and the Auditor's form. Take both to the Auditor first for the endorsement, then to the Recorder in Room 40 before 3:30 PM, or send the packet through an e-recording platform. A cash sale with no lender payoff means no mortgage release to record, so the paperwork is usually just the deed and its transfer form.

Before you go, confirm the deed has the legal description and prior deed reference, that every signature is notarized, and that the page count matches the fee you are bringing. If a document is unusual, such as a trust affidavit or a corrective deed, call 740-852-1854 first so the office can tell you the charge. When the sale involves a rental, remember the landlord filing the Auditor's endorsement points to, and when it involves farmland, ask whether the parcel sits under the agricultural use valuation.

faqs.q: When does Madison County stop recording each day?
faqs.a: 3:30 PM. The office is open until 4 PM on weekdays but stops recording at 3:30, so deliver deeds earlier in the afternoon or use an e-recording service.

faqs.q: What is Madison County's price for recording a deed?
faqs.a: A two-page deed is $39.00 and each extra page is $8.00. Check with the office for extra charges that apply to references, copies or special filings.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Madison County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder names CSC eRecording, Simplifile, ePN and Hopdox as the electronic routes. Ask your title company or attorney which one they use.

faqs.q: Does the Madison County Auditor have a form for a trust or estate transfer?
faqs.a: The forms page lists DTE 100EX for exemption reasons and affidavits for a trustee or successor trustee under Revised Code sections 317.22 and 5302.171. An attorney should pick the right ones for your situation.

faqs.q: How old are Madison County's scanned deeds?
faqs.a: Deeds are scanned, indexed and online from March 1, 1920 forward. Mortgages are scanned and indexed from September 25, 1968, and the original books stay in the office.
